solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Explorer primarily in Antarctica, sick if such a C

definitions.note: throughout this puzzle C stands for colour; a fuchsia is a vivid purplish pink

parts.note: Sir Vivian Fuchs led the Commonwealth Trans-Antarctic Expedition

indicators.note: primarily says take only the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A polar explorer's queasy reaction to something pink, as if the colour itself made him ill.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour in every clue here. The clue has a second route too: 'sick' marks a reshuffle of IF SUCH A, which spells the same seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the flowering shrub, this vivid purplish-pink shade is a recognised colour.

clue.text: Woolly tuft of hair in which flerovium is found? That's not right

parts.note: Fl is the chemical symbol of flerovium

indicators.note: not says the letter for right is left out of the verb

parts.note: something that is found somewhere occurs there

explanation.surface: A query whether a heavy element could turn up in a tuft of wool, quickly dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not right' does the work: 'not' removes R from OCCURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Floccus is the botanical and zoological term for a tuft of woolly hairs.

clue.text: Welsh band in state of stupor, getting lost for a short time in Spanish district

indicators.note: for says one letter takes the place of another

parts.words: Welsh band in state of stupor
parts.note: Catatonia was a Welsh rock band, named after the state of stupor
a short time is time cut to its abbreviation T
L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports results tables

explanation.surface: A Welsh band in a stupor gets lost briefly while touring Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Catatonia was a 1990s Welsh rock band; the band's name is also the stupor. 'for' puts L in place of the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia is an autonomous region in north-east Spain, around Barcelona.

clue.text: French novelist's C, initially seen in beach area

parts.note: George Sand was a French novelist, and sand is also a pale yellowish colour

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of seen

explanation.surface: A French writer's favourite shade first spotted on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour; George Sand was a nineteenth-century French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The sands are the stretch of sandy shore on a beach.

clue.text: C in French inn, keeping cool

indicators.note: keeping says the inn word holds the word for cool inside it

parts.note: auberge is French for an inn
in means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: A colour scheme in a French inn that stays cool.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is the dark purple shade of the vegetable known in America as eggplant.

clue.text: Drinks with county teams' wingers

parts.note: Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

indicators.note: wingers are the players out on the flanks, so take the two edge letters of the word teams'

explanation.surface: Footballers from a county side enjoying red wine together, wingers included.
explanation.walkthrough: County Clare is in Ireland. 'wingers' picks the outside letters, T and S, of 'teams'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarets are red Bordeaux wines, so they are drinks in the plural.

clue.text: C of élite group

definitions.meaning: here C stands for colour: a pale yellowish-white shade
the best people of a set, as in the top of the crop

explanation.surface: The colour favoured by the in-crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream is an off-white colour and also the best part of anything, like the top of the milk.

clue.text: Colleague ordering tea cosies (American not English)

indicators.note: ordering says the letters are arranged afresh
American not English says A takes the place of E

explanation.surface: An office worker buying tea cosies, with a note about transatlantic taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American not English' swaps an E in TEA COSIES for A; 'ordering' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate is a partner or co-worker in a business.

clue.text: Muslim ruler stuck up in tree, methinks

indicators.note: stuck up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sultan stranded up a tree, the speaker suspects.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'stuck up' reads the letters from bottom to top; 'in' marks them as lying inside TREE, METHINKS.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer, more often spelt emir, is a Muslim prince or commander.

clue.text: C of 5 across, roughly

indicators.note: roughly says the letters are rearranged loosely

parts.note: 5 across is the answer to the clue 5 across, red wines

explanation.surface: A rough description of the shade of some red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour. 'roughly' reshuffles the letters of the 5 across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red colour.

clue.text: See 27
Mild or bitter to a novel degree in Israeli town

parts.note: mild and bitter are both styles of British ale
She is the adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A barroom debate about ale styles, settled in a town in Israel with a strangely literary flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild and bitter are British beer styles; 'She' is Rider Haggard's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Beersheba is a city in the Negev desert of southern Israel.

clue.text: Yellow secretion from nipples, as first bits of milk sometimes this C, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the gathered letters may be arranged some other way
first bits of says take the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

parts.note: throughout this puzzle C stands for colour

explanation.surface: A frank note on breastfeeding: the first milk can come out an odd yellowish shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' reshuffles MST (from 'first bits of') together with COLOUR, the word C stands for here.
explanation.definitionFit: Colostrum is the first, yellowish fluid a mother's breasts produce after birth, before true milk comes in.

clue.text: C of fossil fuel? That's about right

indicators.note: about says the fuel word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: coal is the classic fossil fuel

explanation.surface: Someone asking what shade a lump of fuel is and being told they have it about right.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange shade named after the reef-building marine material.

clue.text: Instrument Yes then used, after twice dropping Ecstasy

indicators.note: used, in the sense of worn or knocked about, signals that the remaining letters are rearranged
dropping says those letters are removed from the words Yes then
twice says the drug letter is taken two times over

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A prog-rock story: the band Yes brought in electronic keyboards once they had given up their drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes is a prog-rock band, which makes 'Yes' look like a name. 'dropping' with 'twice' takes both Es out of YES THEN; 'used' rearranges what is left, YSTHN.
explanation.definitionFit: A synth is a synthesiser, an electronic keyboard instrument.

clue.text: C can dry out, leading to public outburst

parts.note: throughout this puzzle C stands for colour, and a hue is a colour

indicators.note: out says the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A tin can drying out sparks a public protest.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour. 'out' rearranges CAN DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue and cry was originally the shout to chase a criminal; now it means a loud public outcry.

clue.text: Not willing to compromise, lacking knowledge en route?

indicators.note: lacking says a word for knowledge is removed from the longer word

parts.note: someone not willing to compromise is intransigent
gen is British slang for information or knowledge

explanation.surface: A stubborn, ill-informed traveller somewhere mid-journey.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or people still travelling between departure and destination are described as being on the way, in transit.

clue.text: C in C, one wearing a sort of green

parts.note: C stands for colour throughout; tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: wearing says the jumbled colour goes round the letter for one
a sort of says the colour word is jumbled into another arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A colour within a colour, the numeral one dressed in a kind of green.
explanation.walkthrough: The first C is the definition and the second is wordplay. 'a sort of' scrambles the colour word to GERNE, and 'wearing' wraps that round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerine is a deep orange shade named after the citrus fruit.

clue.text: System for naming notes taken on Irish hill showing gas-emitting volcanic vent

parts.note: sol-fa is the system that names musical notes doh, ray, me and so on
the Hill of Tara in County Meath was the seat of Ireland's High Kings

explanation.surface: A choir taking its sight-singing up an Irish hill that turns out to be a smoking vent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hill of Tara is the ancient seat of Ireland's High Kings.
explanation.definitionFit: A solfatara is a volcanic vent emitting sulphurous gases and steam.

clue.text: Mouldy lemon? Each one can change its C

indicators.note: mouldy suggests going bad and changing form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rotting lemon that keeps changing colour, like a lizard of shifting hue.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour. 'Mouldy' reshuffles LEMON with EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: This lizard is famous for shifting its skin colour to match its surroundings or mood.

clue.text: Dressed in 5 down C

indicators.note: dressed, as in prepared like a dressed salad, signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 5 down answer, an off-white colour and an elite group

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in cream, wearing one colour.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour. 'Dressed' reshuffles IN with the 5 down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a deep crimson-red shade, originally a pigment from cochineal.

clue.text: Sacré bleu! Wrong cab's gone off for mathematician

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of the French oath are jumbled
gone off says the letters of cab's leave the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: A Frenchman swearing as his taxi drives off without him, wrong way and all.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of CABS away from SACREBLEU and 'Wrong' rearranges what is left, ELEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was the great eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician.

clue.text: C, crossover actor/director

parts.note: throughout this puzzle C stands for colour; red is a colour
a ford is a shallow place to cross over a river

explanation.surface: A film star who crossed over from acting to directing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossover' looks like it describes the career change; it is a ford across a river. C means colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Redford is a Hollywood actor who also directs films, winning an Oscar for Ordinary People.

clue.text: Shop displaying five scores by the Gunners

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners, is the RA
five scores make a hundred, which is a ton

explanation.surface: A sports shop showing five Arsenal results, the club being nicknamed the Gunners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' is a verb here: to inform on someone. Arsenal football club's nickname is the Gunners, but RA is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to shop someone is to betray them to the police, to inform on them.

clue.text: C slightly, as part of getting exasperated

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone colouring up a little as their temper frays.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour, so 'C slightly' is a faint colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour, a faint tint.

clue.text: Old man in dull and boring C, by Vandyke?

parts.note: grey is a colour, and also means dull and boring
a Vandyke is a pointed beard of the kind painted by Van Dyck

explanation.surface: An elderly man dressed in drab clothes, posing for a Van Dyck portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour. 'Vandyke' looks like the painter, but it is the pointed beard named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A greybeard is an old man, named for the grey whiskers of age.

clue.text: Japanese elder statesmen appearing regularly in green (or not)

indicators.note: appearing regularly says take every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Old Japanese politicians keep turning up in green, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing regularly' takes the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of GREEN OR NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The genro were the senior statesmen who advised the Japanese emperor in the Meiji and Taisho eras.

clue.text: C of raging 4, after a dodgy run- out

indicators.note: raging says the letters of the referred-to colour are thrown about
out says the letters of a run leave the pool

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer to 4 down, a dark purple

explanation.surface: A cricket image: an angry colour after a dubious run-out.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour. 'out' takes A, R, U, N from the 4 down answer and 'raging' reshuffles the rest, EBIGE. A run-out is a cricket dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beige is a pale sandy fawn colour.

clue.text: Religious leader serving once, innit?

indicators.note: serving, as in serving up a dish, signals the letters are rearranged and presented anew

explanation.surface: A street-slang aside about a churchman who used to be in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'innit' is British slang for 'isn't it'. 'serving' rearranges ONCE INNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent I was an early Pope, bishop of Rome in the fifth century.

clue.text: Wanderer had a house somewhere in the US

parts.note: Wanderer is the setter, so the setter had is I had, shortened to I'd

explanation.surface: The setter recalls once owning a home in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Wanderer is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Wanderer had' is I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-west of the United States, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Forty-one? Eve's knackered from time to time

indicators.note: knackered is British slang for worn out or broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exhausted Eve, now forty-one, past her prime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knackered' (British for exhausted) rearranges FORTY ONE EVES.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally, at irregular intervals, now and then.

clue.text: C of space-time, extremely lurid

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: extremely says take the two end letters of lurid

explanation.surface: A garish sci-fi shade belonging to space-time itself.
explanation.walkthrough: C means colour. 'space-time' looks like one physics term, but its two halves work separately: an em is a printer's space.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green shade named after the gemstone.
